newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-HEAT DENY BULLS 70TH VICTORY WITH 60TH WIN.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-HEAT DENY BULLS 70TH VICTORY WITH 60TH WIN.

text.p: The Miami Heat picked up their franchise-record 60th win and denied the Chicago Bulls a 70th victory of the season with a 102-92 triumph in a battle of the top two teams in the Eastern Conference on Wednesday.
Jamal Mashburn had 23 points, Tim Hardaway added 22 and Alonzo Mourning 21 as Miami coach Pat Riley reached the 60-win plateau for the seventh time with his third different team.
"Against Chicago, you have to have your best players playing well. I think Jamal had an extraordinary night, along with 'Zo and Tim," Riley said.
"It's a great accomplishment this year, the players should feel good about it," Riley said of winning 60 games. "But in a week, it won't matter because we'll have another challenge ahead of us."
Scottie Pippen scored 28 points and Michael Jordan added 26 for Chicago, which must win their final game -- against New York on Saturday -- to record consecutive 70-win seasons.
"We needed to come out and play hard like this tonight," Hardaway said. "I've never won 60 games or my division. It feels great to me, I'm ecstatic."
In New York, Patrick Ewing had 24 points and 10 rebounds to lead the Knicks to a 96-92 win over the Atlanta Hawks in a head-to-head battle for the third playoff spot in the East.

Allan Houston scored 18 points and John Starks added 11 for the Knicks, who moved into a tie for third place with the Hawks but hold the tiebreaker over Atlanta if the teams finish with identical records.
"I thought we played a great game tonight," Ewing said. "We needed it. This was big for us.
"Now our goal is to win the last two games and head into the playoffs on a high note. We are ready to rock and roll."
Steve Smith scored 33 points to pace the Hawks.

At Washington, Rod Strickland had 34 points and 13 assists as the Bullets moved a step closer to clinching their first playoff berth in nine years with a 103-90 victory over the Indiana Pacers, who were eliminated from playoff contention.
Juwan Howard scored 25 points and Chris Webber added 20 and 12 rebounds for the Bullets, who maintained a one-game lead over Cleveland for the eighth and final playoff berth in the East.
Dale Davis scored 20 points and Jalen Rose added 17 for Indiana, which will miss the playoffs for the first time since 1988.
In Cleveland, Chris Mills and Tyrone Hill each scored 19 points as the Cavaliers kept alive their playoff hopes with a 78-63 victory over the Orlando Magic.
Bob Sura added 14 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists for the Cavs, who remained one game behind Washington for the final playoff spot in the East.
Horace Grant scored 14 points and Nick Anderson added 11 for the Magic, who had their four-game winning streak snapped.
In Portland, Gary Trent scored 20 points and Kenny Anderson added 16 as the Trail Blazers crushed the Denver Nuggets 107-63.
Anderson had seven of his points in the first quarter, just one less than the entire Denver team, who were held to a franchise-low eight points in the opening period and 22 for the first half.
Dontonio Wingfield added 13 points for the Blazers, who led 27-8 after one quarter and 53-22 at halftime.
In Detroit, Theo Ratliff scored a career-high 25 points and Aaron McKie added 18 to lead the Pistons to a 92-85 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks.
Ratliff and McKie also pulled down 12 rebounds each for Detriot, which played without All-Star Grant Hill, who sat out with an ankle injury after recording triple-doubles in his previous three games.
Glenn Robinson scored 25 points for Milwaukee.

In Boston, Glen Rice scored 25 points and Ricky Pierce added 23 as the Charlotte Hornets strengthened their hold on the fifth playoff spot in the East with a 108-102 victory over the woeful Boston Celtics.
Tony Delk chipped in 18 for Charlotte, which leads sixth-place Detroit by one game.
David Wesley scored 25 points and Antoine Walker recorded his first career triple-double with 23 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists for Boston, which suffered its 66th defeat.

At New Jersey, Jerry Stackhouse scored 34 points and Clarence Weatherspoon made a pair of clutch jumpers down the stretch as the Philadelphia 76ers ended an eight-game slide with a 113-105 victory over the Nets.
Allen Iverson was held to 27 points, snapping his rookie record of five straight games scoring at least 40 points.
Kerry Kittles scored 26 points and Kendall Gill added 24 for New Jersey.
At Minnesota, Michael Finley scored five of his 19 points during a pivotal 10-0 burst midway through the fourth quarter as the Dallas Mavericks beat the Timberwolves 92-77.
The win broke an eight-game road losing streak for Dallas, which has gone 18 games without reaching 100 points.
Kevin Garnett had 16 points and Stephon Marbury added 14 for Minnesota, which must win its final two contests to finish at .500 for the first time in franchise history.
